exposure: Previous uterine surgery (including prior C-section and/or myomectomy)
outcome: Mode of birth (C-section vs. normal vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 68,944 women with deliveries over four years, from June 1, 2020, to May 1, 2025, in a tertiary care setting.
finding: The overall C-section rate was 55.0%, with previous uterine surgery (56.2%) being the most common indication, followed by foetal distress (24.3%).
mod_finding: Compared with women who had a normal vaginal delivery, those undergoing C-section had significantly higher percentages of male neonates, maternal age >35 years, multiparity, all categories of preterm birth, early-term birth, low birth weight, and macrosomia.
birth_weight: Included factors: low birth weight, macrosomia
gest_age: Included factors: preterm birth, early-term birth
